input.spec:
Fix round 1 for held T-0073 (spec review T-0074 request_changes). This spec is the T-0073 spec verbatim (B1..B7) plus amendments H1..H11; where H and B disagree, H wins. Start from goal/T-0001 (pnpm install first; leave no untracked files in the worktree).

U3 v5: card backup and restore for signed-in users. Replaces the two-way outbox sync design (T-0056 line), which failed spec review three times on last-write-wins, cursors and a needed migration. This version needs NO migration and has NO timestamp comparison.

Context (on goal/T-0001 at 04f000c): src/sync/supabase.ts exports getSupabase(), isSupabaseConfigured(), withSession(fn(client, userId)) (returns null when signed out/unconfigured; refreshes an expiring session). src/auth/auth.tsx exports AuthProvider, useAuth() {status, userId, ...} and AuthContext. Cards live in src/srs/store.ts (localStorage key alltag.cards; Card in src/lib/types.ts). Table public.items (supabase/migrations/20261010120000_init.sql, ALREADY APPLIED on the live project, do not edit): id uuid pk, user_id text default current_user_id(), noun_fr, phrase_fr not null, phrase_en, error_type, srs jsonb, kept_at timestamptz, updated_at (server trigger sets now()), deleted_at. RLS: user_id = auth.jwt() sub. Row type ItemRow in src/sync/schema.ts.

Behaviour:
B1 Mapping (src/sync/backup.ts, pure + tested): cardToRow(card, userId) -> {id, user_id, noun_fr ?? null, phrase_fr, phrase_en ?? null, error_type: errorType ?? null, srs: {interval, ease, reps, due: ISO of card.due, learnedAt: ISO of card.learnedAt, objectId?, place?}, kept_at: ISO of learnedAt, deleted_at: null}. rowToCard(row) is the inverse (ISO -> epoch ms; invalid/missing numbers fall back to the keep() defaults ease 2.5, interval 0, reps 0, due now). crop is NEVER sent or restored (photos stay on the device). Only cards whose id is a UUID (regex) are backed up; others are skipped. Extend SrsState in schema.ts with optional learnedAt, objectId, place (jsonb, no SQL change).
B2 Store hooks (src/srs/store.ts, minimal additions, existing exports unchanged): subscribe(fn) -> unsubscribe, called after every save; addRestored(cards) appends cards whose id is not present and whose (noun_fr defined, noun_fr, errorType) key does not match a local card, returns the number added, notifies once; tombstones: remove(id) and clear() record the removed UUID ids in localStorage key alltag.cards.removed (same storage fallback pattern); pendingRemovals() and ackRemovals(ids).
B3 Backup run (backup.ts runBackup()): inside withSession: (a) for pending removals, client.from("items").update({deleted_at: new Date().toISOString()}).in("id", ids) then ackRemovals on success; (b) upsert all local UUID cards via cardToRow in chunks of 200 with onConflict "id". Single flight: a run requested while one is running sets a dirty flag and reruns once after. Errors (returned {error} or thrown) never throw out of runBackup; they set status "error". When navigator.onLine is false, skip and set status "offline".
B4 Restore (backup.ts runRestore()): inside withSession: select id,noun_fr,phrase_fr,phrase_en,error_type,srs,kept_at from items where deleted_at is null (RLS scopes to the user); skip ids in pending removals; store.addRestored(rows.map(rowToCard)); then runBackup(). Device wins: never overwrite a local card.
B5 Runner (src/sync/BackupRunner.tsx, rendered inside AuthProvider in src/main.tsx, renders nothing): when useAuth().status becomes "signed_in" -> runRestore() once per signed-in userId. While signed in: store.subscribe -> debounce 3000 ms -> runBackup(); window "online" -> runBackup(); after an "error" retry once per 60 s while signed in. Cleans up all timers/listeners on sign-out/unmount. Disabled/signed_out: does nothing, no network.
B6 Status: backup.ts exports a tiny observable status {state: "off"|"working"|"ok"|"error"|"offline", lastOkAt: number|null} and useBackupStatus(). Settings signed-in account section adds one line: "backed up HH:MM" (24 h) when ok, "backing up…" when working, "backup failed, will retry" on error, "offline, will back up later" when offline. Nothing else in Settings changes.
B7 Docs: docs/SUPABASE.md and README get one short paragraph: signed-in cards are backed up to your account and restored on a new device; photos and conversations stay on the device; reset on a device also removes the backup.
Rollback: git revert the commit; no schema or live change (rows written to items are user data and stay).

Amendments (H wins over B):
H1 Deletes propagate (T-0074 risk 1). Before the upsert, runBackup checks the server for deleted rows among the local UUID ids: select id from items where deleted_at is not null and id in (chunk) in chunks of 100 ids. Ids found are (a) excluded from the upsert and (b) removed locally through a new store method dropRemote(ids): removes those cards, records NO tombstone, notifies once. A card removed on device A therefore disappears from device B on B's next backup instead of being revived. Trade-off, stated in docs: grades made on a stale device for a card deleted elsewhere are lost. Test: a local card whose server row has deleted_at set is not upserted and is gone from store.all() after runBackup; a card with deleted_at null is upserted as before.
H2 Tombstones and local cards on a user change (risk 2). New localStorage key alltag.backup.owner holds the userId of the last restore or backup on this device (same storage fallback). In the runner, on signed_in with userId: if owner is set and differs, ackRemovals(all pending) first (the previous owner's tombstones never run under the new account), then owner = userId. Local cards are kept and backed up into the new account (device wins; documented: "signing in with a different account on this device adds this device's cards to that account"). Tombstones recorded while signed out or with owner unset run at the next sign-in (ids the account does not own are no-ops under RLS and are acked). Test: owner A, pending removals, sign in as B: no update call, removals acked, owner is B, local cards upserted under B.
H3 Paging and chunking (risk 3). Removal updates run in chunks of 100 ids; each chunk is acked only after its own update succeeded, failed chunks stay pending. The restore select is ordered by id and paged with .range(from, from + 999) until a page returns fewer than 1000 rows. The H1 deleted check is chunked at 100. Test: restore over a fake client returning 1000 then 500 rows adds 1500 cards; 250 removals make 3 update calls and a failure in the second acks only the first chunk.
H4 Restore retry (risk 4). runRestore checks navigator.onLine first (false: status offline, no network, nothing acked). The runner keeps restoredFor: userId | null, set only when the restore select completed successfully. The "online" handler and the retry timer call runRestore while restoredFor !== userId, otherwise runBackup. runBackup after a restore runs only when the select succeeded. Test: restore select fails (status error), then an "online" event calls runRestore again, and after that success further events call runBackup only.
H5 Upsert error policy and backoff (risk 5). Upsert chunks run in order; a failed chunk is recorded and the remaining chunks still run; the run ends in status error if any chunk failed, ok otherwise. Tombstone acks depend only on their own update (H3), never on the upsert. Error retry: 60 s after the first failed run, doubling per consecutive failure up to 600 s, reset to 60 s after an ok run. Test: two failing chunks out of three still upsert the third; with fake timers the second retry fires at 120 s and the cap is 600 s.
H6 Status transitions (risk 6). withSession returning null sets {off, lastOkAt: null}. The runner resets status to {off, lastOkAt: null} on signed_out, disabled, a userId change and unmount, and exports resetBackupStatus() from backup.ts for that. Test in BackupRunner.test.tsx: ok -> sign out -> status off with lastOkAt null.
H7 Mapping edges and dedupe (risk 7). rowToCard turns null noun_fr, phrase_en and error_type into omitted fields (undefined), never null, so addRestored's noun_fr check and keep()'s byNoun agree. addRestored also dedupes within the incoming batch by id and by the (noun_fr, errorType) key, first row wins. A local card that matches a server row only by key keeps its own id and is still uploaded; cross-device duplicates of the same noun are accepted and documented. Device wins is stated in the docs: a restored card never overwrites local SRS state; the server copy is only used when the card is missing on this device. Test: a batch with two rows of the same noun and errorType adds one; a row with null noun_fr restores to a card without noun_fr.
H8 Diffed upsert and tombstone cap (risk 8). backup.ts keeps an in-memory map id -> JSON of the last successfully upserted row for the current owner (cleared on owner change and resetBackupStatus). A run upserts only cards whose cardToRow JSON differs from that map or are not in it; cards added by addRestored are entered into the map as uploaded, so the backup after a restore sends nothing for them. A run with no changed rows makes no upsert call and still sets ok. alltag.cards.removed keeps at most 2000 ids, oldest dropped. Test: second runBackup with no change performs no upsert; one grade() then runBackup upserts exactly one row; the 2001st tombstone drops the oldest.
H9 schema.ts (risk 9). The header comment says Supabase Auth (JWT sub), not Clerk; SrsState additions are optional so src/sync/supabase.test.ts and other ItemRow consumers type-check unchanged.
H10 Reset caveat (risk 10). Settings reset copy and behaviour stay as they are. The docs paragraph adds: a reset made while offline or signed out removes the backup the next time this device backs up signed in to the same account. Rollback note in docs/SUPABASE.md: after a git revert the localStorage keys alltag.cards.removed and alltag.backup.owner are harmless leftovers, and deleted_at values already written stay.
H11 Scope check (T-0074 suggestion). The gate also checks git diff --stat goal/T-0001..HEAD: only the scoped paths changed; supabase/migrations/**, package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml unchanged.

Tests (vitest, mock @supabase via the supabase.ts seam: vi.mock of "./supabase" withSession or a fake client; spread vi.importActual where a real export is needed):
- backup.test.ts: mapping round trip (crop dropped, dates ISO <-> ms, defaults on bad srs, nulls to omitted fields); non-UUID ids skipped; upsert chunks of 200 with onConflict id; removals in chunks of 100 acked per chunk only on success; error and thrown error set status error and do not throw; failed chunk does not stop later chunks; offline skip; single flight with one rerun; H1 server-deleted ids skipped and dropped locally; H8 diffed upsert; restore paged over 1000 rows, adds missing cards, skips local-id and same noun+errorType duplicates (also in-batch) and pending removals, then backs up only after a successful select; withSession null sets off.
- store.test.ts additions: subscribe fires after keep/grade/remove/clear/addRestored/dropRemote; addRestored dedupe (local and in-batch) and count; dropRemote removes without tombstone; tombstones recorded on remove/clear for UUID ids only and capped at 2000; existing store tests pass unchanged.
- BackupRunner.test.tsx: signed_in triggers one restore per user; failed restore retried on "online" until success, then backup only; a store change triggers backup after 3000 ms (fake timers); retry backoff 60 s, 120 s, cap 600 s; owner change acks pending removals and resets the uploaded map; signed_out does nothing and resets status to off; cleanup on unmount.
- Settings.test.tsx: the four status lines in the signed-in section; existing tests pass unchanged.
